guide.supabaseTitle: Guide · your own free Supabase database
guide.author: Author
guide.supabaseLead: LingQ translation works without a database. You need Supabase only for Dictionary, Import, Stats and Latency. The free plan on supabase.com is enough.
guide.supabaseWarn: Warning: installing, updating or manually editing SQL can damage database data (deleting / changing tables and functions). Before changing a DB already in use, back up the project in Supabase if possible. Run only SQL from this extension and only if you know what you are doing.
guide.supabaseSteps:
• Open supabase.com → Start your project and create an account (GitHub, Google or email).
  • Create a new project (New project), choose a nearby region, set a database password and wait until it is Ready.
  • In the project open Project Settings → API. Copy the Project URL and the anon / publishable key (public key, not service_role).
  • In the extension, open Settings and paste the URL and publishable key (you can save settings right away).
  • Check: click Check database. The extension verifies tables, functions and schema version and reports whether the DB is OK or what is missing.
  • Install / update from clipboard:
    1. Click Install / update database — SQL is copied to the clipboard and the Supabase SQL Editor opens.
    2. Click in the empty editor field and paste: Ctrl+V (Windows) or Cmd+V (Mac).
    3. Run the script with Run (or Ctrl+Enter). Wait until it finishes without errors.
    4. Return to the extension and click Check database again — it should say the database is ready.
  • After updating the extension, use Check again; if it reports an older schema, run the clipboard install again. You can also run files in the supabase/ folder manually (including schema_version.sql).
guide.supabaseNote: The publishable key cannot run SQL directly — that is why install goes through the clipboard and SQL Editor. After a successful check you do not need to manage the database from the browser; the extension stores data itself.
guide.chatgptWarn: Note: the ChatGPT API is paid. You pay for tokens used according to OpenAI pricing — this is not a ChatGPT Plus subscription. The extension works without this key (LingQ); you need the key only for ChatGPT translations / alternatives.
guide.chatgptSteps:
• Open platform.openai.com and sign in (or create an OpenAI account).
  • In account / billing settings add a payment method and credit — without credit the API usually does not work.
  • Go to API keys → Create new secret key, copy the key immediately (it will not be shown again).
  • In the extension Settings paste the key into the ChatGPT API key field and save. Then you can choose ChatGPT as the source for new words / more translations and pick a model.

import.help: Imports vocabulary cards and known words (both sets). Cards first (with translation from hints), then known words — even those without translation are saved with an empty translation. Existing card translations are not overwritten. Batches of max 5,000 with a 1 h pause between them. Run supabase/import_known_words.sql once.

help.phraseChatgpt: ChatGPT translates sentences with no length limit. In the user build, LingQ would apply a 10-word limit.
